8NotePLAN. Baseline m1 (nominal): real reads ~+4.6..6.5 C above model r1. Low-power m2: +1.9..3.3 C above r2. Diff scales with power -> multiplicative (~+16% on rise above ambient), not offset. Fidelity gap 0.49 C so this is a real fault. Per-sensor ratio (real rise / model rise, amb 42): nominal c0 1.138 c1 1.155 c2 1.149 c3 1.139 c4 1.168 c5 1.135 c6 1.181 c7 1.194 pkg 1.205; low: 1.145 1.159 1.154 1.112 1.170 1.166 1.187 1.171 1.169. Pattern stable across proportional workloads (but my 2 workloads were proportional, so can't yet separate sensor-gain vs block-wise model fault). Spread beyond quantization noise -> NOT one single global fault; there is per-sensor or per-region structure. Next: (a) read all at high power (already set, proportional 3rd point); (b) LEFT-heavy workload; (c) RIGHT-heavy workload -> per-sensor ratio invariance across power distributions separates sensor gain faults (invariant) from block power/thermal faults (varies); (d) transient to test time constants (R-fault changes tau, power-fault doesn't) and capacitance faults.
9Propose h1Real chip runs ~16% hotter (rise above ambient) than model predicts, multiplicative in power (diff scales with power, not an offset). Cause could be global power_gain error, global conductance error, or sensor gain errors.
10Propose h2Right-side sensors (core4, core6, core7, package) show systematically larger error (~1.17-1.21) than left-side (core0, core3, core5 ~1.11-1.14): possible regional model fault on right-side blocks, or per-sensor gain faults.

53NoteREFIT. Repaired (x1.18) steady residuals: nominal all +0.3..+0.7, m3 high c2 +2.2 (real 93 vs model 90.8), m5 right-heavy c6/c7 +1.7/+1.5, m4 left-heavy c4-c7 +1.6..+2.1, c0..c3 mostly +0.3..+0.9, pkg -0.5..+2.1. Most sensors under-predict by +0.5-1C in ALL workloads, plus larger under-prediction (~+2C) in high-power regions. This is consistent with the x1.18 being too small a correction. Also TRANSIENT: real settles faster (tau~0.35) than repaired model (tau~0.58): real T_core2 reaches 80C at t=0.68, model at t=0.76; real reaches 85C at t=1.28, model at t=2.8. Higher R AND faster settling => real C is LOWER than model C. Real tau/R ratio suggests C_real ~ 0.6x model C. Alternative: real dynamics could be faster because die-level (not boundary) resistances are the fast mode and boundary R change doesn't alter the fast die-settling mode; need care. The fast initial rise (t<0.2) is die-spreading; both show similar early rise 63->76 at t=0.4 (real) vs 73.3 (model) — actually REAL RISES FASTER EARLY TOO: real t(73)=0.32, model t(73.3)=0.40. So real is faster everywhere => real C lower. Estimate: real tau ~ 0.6x model tau while R_real ~ 1.18x R_model => C_real ~ 0.51x C_model. That's a large capacitance fault. But wait — a C fault does NOT affect steady state. Steady under-prediction of +0.5-2C means R factor > 1.18. Candidates: boundary R factor larger (say 1.25) + C fault, OR the fault could be in die-to-IHS edges too. Next: use steady residuals to refit boundary factor via sensitivity runs, then test transient with adjusted C.
54Measuretransient on T_core0, workload 69.6 W total80
55NoteTransient re-analysis (normalized by each curve's own rise): real and repaired-model dynamics actually MATCH within quantization+transient gap for both core0 and core2. My earlier 'faster settling' alarm was an artifact of comparing absolute crossing times when finals differed. NO capacitance fault. Remaining issue: per-sensor steady residuals after x1.18 repair: c0 ~+0.3, c3 ~-0.1, c5 ~+0.7, pkg ~+1.0 (within sensor spec: 3% slope=1.1C at nominal, noise 0.5, quant 0.5, cal 0.3) BUT c2 ~+1.5, c4 ~+1.9, c6 ~+1.8, c7 ~+2.0, c1 ~+1.1 consistently positive, ~4-6% of rise, exceeding spec. Two rival explanations: (a) sensor gain faults on c2/c4/c6/c7 (c1 borderline); (b) per-block model faults on those blocks' boundary/vertical R; (c) global f larger (~1.22) with c0/c3/c5/pkg reading low. DECISIVE TEST: single-block-max workloads (core4-max, core7-max, core2-max, rest at min). A model R-fault on core4 raises T_core4 AND neighbors (heat spreads); a sensor gain raises ONLY T_core4's own reading. Also per-block fault signature scales with heat through that block's boundary; sensor gain scales with sensor's own rise only.

82Propose h3Global model fault: the model's IHS-to-ambient boundary conductances are too high by a uniform factor ~1.22 (model R too low; real die runs ~22% hotter in rise above ambient). Repairing all 13 boundary edges R×1.22 reproduces every workload within the steady gap + sensor spec. Mechanism verified as boundary (not power-gain or per-block): non-proportional workloads (m4/m5/m8/m9) fit boundary-R repair with rms 0.8°C while a uniform power-gain fit leaves ±2.3°C spread at m5; single-block faults and per-sensor gain faults were ruled out by remote-excess analysis.
83Prune h1Absorbed into h3: the ~16% underprediction is now precisely attributed to the global boundary-conductance fault (factor ~1.22) and repaired; no separate mechanism remains.
84Prune h2Right-side 'regional' pattern was an artifact of the single global factor fit; after the x1.22 boundary repair, right-side sensors fall within sensor-spec residuals (c4/c7 ~+1C = 2.7-3% slope, within the 3% spec bound) and the package sensor is unbiased. No regional model fault or per-sensor fault beyond spec.
85Answer 1model · global · All IHS-to-ambient boundary edges are too conductive in the model (boundary resistance too low), so the real die runs ~22% hotter in temperature rise above ambi · 0.22✗ wrong
